description: I am looking to collaborate with creative developers, designers, and problem-solvers who are passionate about space tech, game mechanics, and simulation design. If you have experience in frontend/backend development, UI/UX, or game logic, let's build an amazing mission simulation together!
summary:
We developed an interactive educational gaming platform for space mission planning and project management, designed to teach the end-to-end methodology of building a space mission based on official NASA Systems Engineering standards.
The platform simulates the full mission life cycle—from scientific need identification to advancing through JPL Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1–4), conducting trade space studies, passing critical review gates (PDR/CDR), and managing real-time operations. Players actively manage and balance essential project constraints: launch payload mass, financial budget, power distribution, system reliability, and crew wellbeing, while navigating realistic orbital mechanics.
The importance of this project lies in transforming complex systems engineering into an accessible, hands-on learning tool. Featuring an automated feedback engine that delivers root-cause failure analysis and actionable lessons learned, alongside guidance from historical science & NASA mentors, the platform equips players with structured planning methodologies, systems thinking, and practical management skills to successfully execute space missions.
details:
Our project is an interactive simulation game that replicates the end-to-end planning, engineering, and launch of a real space mission—from initial concept to orbital deployment. Structured around NASA’s four Concept Maturity Levels (CMLs), the platform combines deterministic physics calculations (modeled after GMAT for Δ v and trajectory design), live 3D orbital visualization and authentic operational constraints such as regulatory licensing chains (FCC/NOAA), rigid launch windows, and engineering review gates (PDR/CDR/SIR). The project's creativity and core value lie in making complex aerospace systems engineering accessible and engaging: inspired by NASA’s Mission Design Lab (MDL), we integrated an AI advisory team of historical space pioneers (such as Katherine Johnson and Margaret Hamilton) offering real-time guidance, alongside contextual tooltips, a badge system, and a community leaderboard that drive Pareto-optimal trade-offs and competitive replayability. Built with modern web technologies and grounded in official NASA methodologies, our intended impact is to provide students, educators, and space enthusiasts with a realistic, hands-on environment to master multidisciplinary mission design and engineering compromises.

*****

This solution was developed as part of NASA Space Apps Tel Aviv 2026. The event was led by the Space Engineering Center (SEC) and SpaceTAU at Tel Aviv University, in partnership with the Rakia Mission and Space Campus IL.
